detail: A calm pale warm-grey limestone slab. One broad soft-edged-in-design-but-pixel-stepped beige mineral band and very few connected chips, no isolated speckles. Large quiet dominant warm-grey surface. Subtle material variation rather than a flat plastic panel.
prompt:
Create ONE independent production pixel-art material source for a tactical game battlefield. Subject: exactly one complete square ground paving slab, seen in strict orthographic top-down view, fills the entire image. A calm pale warm-grey limestone slab. One broad soft-edged-in-design-but-pixel-stepped beige mineral band and very few connected chips, no isolated speckles. Large quiet dominant warm-grey surface. Subtle material variation rather than a flat plastic panel. Near-modern magical academy limestone courtyard, clean and maintained. Native design intent is about 32 coarse square pixel units across this one metre slab; every mark, mineral band, border and highlight uses that SAME SINGLE uniform square macro-pixel lattice. It is an enlarged genuine low-resolution pixel design, not a high-resolution painting shrunk down. Use deliberate large connected pixel clusters, no small texture. Keep one dominant stone color across at least half the slab, at most three broad internal darker material clusters and a limited cohesive palette of at most eight flat colors. A clear thin border on ALL FOUR sides, exactly one macro-pixel thick in the stone's own darker warm-grey (never black); a thin pale inner lip only one macro-pixel thick, aligned to the very same lattice. Interior is nearly flat; edge framing marks a tactical cell, not a raised block. All pixels are square, crisp hard edges, stepped shape boundaries, zero anti-aliasing, gradients, dithering or fine detail. Neutral flat even diffuse illumination. Solid opaque material, full-bleed square image; no surroundings, margins, perspective, facade, multiple tiles, grid overlay, labels, words, watermark, objects, seams dividing the interior into smaller tiles, cast shadows, circular shadows, glow, vignette, wet specular highlights or final color grading. The player's units must remain visually dominant over this calm material.
Critical correction for this independent retry: all the complete square slab's features must be on ONE countable coarse square raster, approximately thirty-two large flat-colored squares per side. Never mix half-size marks into this raster. The outer dark stone frame and inner pale lip are each one WHOLE square pixel unit thick, exactly the same unit as the smallest interior feature, including corners. The dark outer frame touches the four image boundaries; there is no half-unit margin outside it. Stone colors are truly solid flat color fills within each square, with no transparent layering, tonal texture or smooth changes inside a square. Interior material regions consist of a few broad stepped connected masses made from those large square units. Reduce the fine grain; do not add new detail. No isolated tiny pixels, fine mottling, subpixel rectangles or antialiasing.
